title: A background turn launched from under launchd never starts on macOS
foundBy: campaign CI: every smoke podman (macos-arm64) leg since the self-hosted runners came back as LaunchDaemons on 2026-09-21; diagnosed by session agent
details:
**What happened.** On macOS, `cs-<agent>-remote -b` prints `Running:  background (PID unknown)` and the turn never runs. The log holds the prompt header and nothing else, `-output -s` calls the session crashed, and the per-session `.runner` script is left behind unexecuted. In campaign CI, every macOS smoke leg waited out its 15-minute readback with no member having run a turn.

**Why.** The launch SBX-038 added for hosts without `setsid` is `( set -m; nohup "$RUNNER_FILE" … 2>&1 & )`. Apple's `nohup` is not GNU's. It calls `_vprocmgr_detach_from_console` before it execs, and when its caller runs in launchd's system domain, as a LaunchDaemon does, launchd refuses (`Session adoption is only allowed in user domains`). nohup then exits `can't detach from console` without running anything. That message goes to /dev/null with the rest of the launch's output. The self-hosted runners had been started by hand from a login session, where the detach succeeds, and SBX-038 was verified there. So the launch never ran under launchd until the machine rebooted and the runners came back as services.

**Why it matters.** A CI runner, a launchd job, or anything else that drives turns from under launchd on a Mac cannot dispatch a single background turn, and nothing says why.

**How to reproduce.** Run `cs-claude-remote -b` from any process in launchd's system domain on macOS. A self-hosted Actions runner installed with `svc.sh install` is one. The unified log shows `nohup[…] Could not adopt Background session: 125` at the moment of the launch.

**What would help.** Launch with a form that needs no external program, so it behaves the same on every host. `set -m` gives the runner a process group of its own, and the hangup is ignored before the exec rather than by nohup.

notes.text: The three remote tools now launch with `( set -m; trap '' HUP; "$RUNNER_FILE" … & )` on every host, with no setsid and no nohup. On Linux and macOS, with and without a terminal, the runner gets its own process group, ignores SIGHUP, and survives its caller killing its own group. `TestRemoteBackgroundTurnRuns` runs every family with a nohup that fails the way Apple's does under launchd. It fails on the old launch (`PID unknown` for claude, codex and opencode) and passes on the new one. It stays open until a macOS runner, which runs as a LaunchDaemon, passes that test.
